name: Dedicated small-launch price per kg
question: Q1
rationale: 12 M EUR for 700 kg is about 19000 USD/kg; Electron earns about 28000 USD/kg

name: Payload fill rate per launch
question: Q1
rationale: Spectrum flies full: several customers share a launch like a rideshare on Spectrum (bundlers such as SEOPS fill the rest). Team decision 22.10.2026; 60 % was the earlier single-customer view

name: Price per Spectrum launch
question: Q1
rationale: Not published; estimates 10–15 M EUR; NewSpace Index about 10 M USD; Electron earns 8.5 M USD for a third of the capacity

name: Rideshare price per kg
question: Q1
rationale: SpaceX list price 2027; about 10000 USD/kg with separation system

name: Exchange rate
question: Q1
rationale: ECB October 2026 average

name: US government demand open to Isar
question: Q1
rationale: NSPM-17 sends US government payloads to US-built launchers

name: Other governments' demand open to Isar
question: Q1
rationale: Japan, India, Korea and others mostly fly their own launchers

name: Launch sites
question: Q1
rationale: 0 = Andøya only (Q1 today); 1 = plus Nova Scotia (45–98° from 2028); 2 = plus Kourou (low inclinations and GTO)

name: Spectrum launches per year
question: Q1
rationale: Isar's plan for 2027 as its first full operating year; one launch in 2026; production is the bottleneck

name: Share of the serviceable market that buys a dedicated launch
question: Q1
rationale: Measured 2025: 6.7% of SAM satellites (4.2% of mass) flew on a small launcher, all on Rocket Lab's Electron; the rest rode SpaceX rideshare. BryceTech: 10–14% in the West. Planet: new rockets get demo payloads first

name: Launch success rate
question: Q1
rationale: Insurance of about 25% on Isar's next mission implies 75%; mature launchers reach 92–95%

name: Base year of flown demand
question: Q1
rationale: Latest full year; 2024 as comparison shows how much a single year swings

name: Payload per Spectrum load
question: Q2
rationale: Spectrum's 700 kg to SSO × 100 % fill rate (lower bound 60 % fill); load.py checks it against both

name: Spectrum launches planned in 2030
question: Q2
rationale: Team base case from the earlier cadence plan 4/7/10/12 for 2027–2030. Isar publishes only 4 (2027) and about 8 (2028); a 2030 figure is not public

name: Launch success rate 2028
question: Q2
rationale: Ramp between 80 % today (insurance for Isar's next mission about 25 %) and about 92 % for mature small launchers

name: Launch success rate 2030
question: Q2
rationale: Industry 5–8 % failures; Planet saw 3 failures in 44 launches

name: Minimum block of hypersonic test flights
question: Q2
rationale: Only enter suborbital testing with a block buy like Rocket Lab's 20 HASTE flights for 190 M USD; single flights cost Andøya slots

name: Launches per year before a mid-class rocket
question: Q2
rationale: Team setting: a new vehicle class (about 10 years, billions) only after Spectrum proves cadence

name: Success rate before a mid-class rocket
question: Q2
rationale: Team setting: reliability first; new rockets only get demo payloads until proven

name: Yearly Nova Scotia fee anchor customers must cover
question: Q2
rationale: 3.75 M USD per quarter at 1.12 USD/EUR (range from the 1.08–1.17 FX range), plus per-launch fees on a cost-plus basis; expansion only if anchor customers cover it

name: Decision year for Nova Scotia
question: Q2
rationale: End of the 30-month fee waiver that starts after the first contract year; the exact term start is not public

name: Market growth outside megaconstellations
question: Q2+
rationale: Novaspace forecast implies about 9% a year; BryceTech history 13–17%
